hints.title: Test the universal pair claim
hints.body: Statement I compares <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> for every allowed pair. Look for a real number and a positive integer that could challenge the strict inequality <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo><</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></math>.
hints.recap: One permitted pair can disprove a claim about all pairs.
hints.pitfall: A test pair must satisfy both variable domains.
hints.pause: Choose your own pair, check both domains, and decide whether its comparison supports or refutes I.

recall.reminder: One permitted pair can disprove a claim about all pairs.

hints.title: Track a choice that may depend on an input
hints.body: In II, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> is fixed before <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> is chosen. Place a given real input and the positive integers on a number line, then investigate whether an integer choice can satisfy the required comparison. Consider nonpositive and positive inputs separately.
hints.recap: An existential choice made after an input may depend on that input.
hints.pitfall: Do not replace a fresh choice for each input by one fixed integer for all inputs.
hints.pause: Give a construction that works for every permitted input, or produce an input for which no allowed choice works.

recall.reminder: An existential choice made after an input may depend on that input.

hints.title: Find a fixed witness for the reversed order
hints.body: For III, first identify the smallest allowed integer <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></math>. Seek one real <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> whose comparison with that integer will also work for every larger allowed integer.
hints.recap: The same witness must work for every positive integer.
hints.pitfall: Positive integers and all integers have different lower-bound behaviour.
hints.pause: Choose and verify a witness, then assess the three quantified statements.

recall.reminder: The same witness must work for every positive integer.

solution:
I is false: x=2 and n=1 give 2<1.

II is true: if x≤0, choose n=1; otherwise choose an integer strictly larger than x.

III is true with the single choice x=0, since every positive integer exceeds 0. II and III only: answer G.
knowledgePattern: Order of real/integer universal and existential quantifiers
